title: Research
text: My current research examines how agricultural producers and landowners make decisions about adopting conservation programs and management practices. Going forward, I am interested in studying how agricultural, food, and land-use policies influence producer and consumer decisions. I also plan to work on regenerative agriculture, climate-change adaptation, and interdisciplinary studies that integrate economic, agronomic, biophysical, and management data.

title: Faizul Kabir
text:
I am a PhD candidate in the Department of Agricultural Economics at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln. My work broadly lies in environmental and resource economics and behavioral economics, with a focus on how producers and consumers make adoption decisions.
I am currently studying ranchers’ preferences for the Grassland Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) and Conservation pogram associated with it and the role of social networks in conservation program participation and practice adoption in the Northern U.S. Great Plains. Going forward, I am interested to study how agricultural, food, and land-use policies influence producer and consumer decisions. I also plan work on regenerative agriculture, climate-change adaptation, and interdisciplinary studies that integrate economic, agronomic, biophysical, and management data.
I am currently on the job market and open to opportunities in research, policy, and academia.
